clue.text: Stepped back, squashing minute fly

indicators.note: squashing something means pressing it in, so one piece is held inside the other
going back means the word for stepped is read from its end to its start

parts.note: paced means walked with measured steps
M is the abbreviation for minute

explanation.surface: Someone backs away while swatting a tiny insect.
explanation.walkthrough: PACED reversed is DECAP, which squeezes M between its A and P. 'Fly' looks like the insect being squashed; it is the verb meaning flee.
explanation.definitionFit: To decamp is to leave suddenly or secretly, which is one sense of the verb fly, to flee.

clue.text: Obscure English coin

parts.note: to obscure is to make dim
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: An unfamiliar old English coin, of the sort collectors hunt for.
explanation.definitionFit: A dime is the American ten-cent piece, a small coin.

clue.text: Clot's gone astray in California

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the jumbled letters sit inside the state abbreviation
astray means gone off course, so the letters of gone wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A fool has gone off the rails in California.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clot' looks like a British noun for a fool; here it is a verb, to thicken.
explanation.definitionFit: To clot is to thicken into a solid mass, as blood or cream does when it sets.

clue.text: In final move I turned on count

indicators.note: in tells us the next pieces sit inside the chess word for the last move

parts.note: checkmate, the last move of a chess game
taken as written
a lamp that is turned on is lit

explanation.surface: A chess player's final move depended on a count.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count' looks like a noun or a nobleman; it is the verb meaning to carry weight. Checkmate is the move that ends a chess game.
explanation.definitionFit: To militate is to have weight or influence as evidence, which is to count for or against something.

clue.text: Absorbing cuts, diocese returned shrouds

indicators.note: something absorbing another takes it in, so one piece ends up inside the other
returned means sent back, so the bishop's seat is read backwards

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese
clips are cuts, as with shears

explanation.surface: A church diocese, absorbing budget cuts, sends back its burial shrouds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shrouds' looks like a noun for burial cloths; it is a verb meaning covers. A see is the area a bishop governs.
explanation.definitionFit: To eclipse something is to cover or obscure it, as shrouds conceal what they wrap.

clue.text: Rich maestro's alter ego?

indicators.note: to alter is to change, so the letters of the two words are reorganised

parts.note: eleven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A wealthy conductor's other personality is the subject.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also hints at the answer: a choirmaster is a kind of maestro, a musical director, so is in a sense his other self.
explanation.definitionFit: A choirmaster trains and conducts a choir, a musical leader like an orchestral maestro.

clue.text: Swallow with humour, we're told

indicators.note: what we are told we hear spoken, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: a remark made with humour is said in jest

explanation.surface: Accept something good-naturedly, as people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' looks like putting up with a joke; it is the literal act of eating.
explanation.definitionFit: To ingest is to take food or drink into the body, that is, to swallow it.

clue.text: Derisive cry from escort regularly in attendance

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so only every second letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters
someone in attendance is here

explanation.surface: A jeer comes from a companion who keeps showing up.
explanation.definitionFit: So there! is a childish taunting exclamation, a cry of defiance or mockery.

clue.text: Serves, if tea is prepared on board

indicators.note: on, as in on a ship, means aboard, so the reworked letters travel inside the vessel

parts.note: on board conventionally means inside SS, the steamship abbreviation, so board stands for the ship

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, so the letters of if tea is are reworked

explanation.surface: A steward serves passengers if tea is made ready on the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serves' looks like waiting at table, but it means is good enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that serves a need is good enough for it, which is what satisfies means.

clue.text: Capital chap boxer knocked over

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: something knocked over is upended, so the boxer's name runs backwards

parts.note: Muhammad Ali, the most famous boxer

explanation.surface: A splendid fellow, a boxer, gets knocked down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like British slang for excellent describing the chap; it is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Manila is the capital city of the Philippines.

clue.text: Bird following fashion? No chance!

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the bird is placed second, behind the verb for fashion

parts.note: to forge is to fashion, as a smith does
a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: Following the latest bird-related fashion is out of the question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' puts the bird after the verb, not before.
explanation.definitionFit: Forget it! is an emphatic refusal, meaning there is no possibility of that happening.

clue.text: Sound of those putting down Fab Four's stout footwear

indicators.note: the sound of a word is how it is heard, not how it is written

parts.note: the Fab Four were the Beatles; one of them is a Beatle
people who put others down crush them

explanation.surface: Critics of the Beatles have their say about sturdy shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: Beetle-crushers is jocular British slang for large heavy boots, apt for stamping on insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Beetle-crushers are big heavy shoes or boots, the sort of stout footwear that flattens beetles.

clue.text: Constant sound of bell after several breaks

indicators.note: after says the bell's sound comes behind the rearranged letters
breaks means comes apart, so the letters of several are reassembled

parts.note: ting is the light ringing sound of a small bell

explanation.surface: A bell keeps ringing after several breaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Everlasting means lasting for ever, never changing, which is what constant means.

clue.text: Half piglet cooked to make up for the deficiency

indicators.note: cooked means prepared or tampered with, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: all ten letters of both words

explanation.surface: A short meat supply is topped up with half a roast pig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half' looks like an instruction to take half of piglet, but its letters are part of the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To fill the gap is to supply what is missing, which is making up for a shortfall.

clue.text: Famous bridge and when it needs painting?

parts.note: the Forth Bridge, the railway bridge across the Firth of Forth in Scotland
with means along with, and

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a famous bridge and its maintenance schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: Painting the Forth Bridge is a British byword for an endless job: legend says repainting must start again the moment it is finished, so the answer is always now.
explanation.definitionFit: Forthwith means immediately, the time the Forth Bridge supposedly always needs repainting.

clue.text: One type of lighting rejected by shop

indicators.note: rejected suggests being turned back, so the pieces are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
LED, a light-emitting diode

explanation.surface: A shop has turned down a particular kind of lighting.
explanation.definitionFit: A deli, short for delicatessen, is a shop selling cooked meats, cheeses and other prepared foods.

clue.text: Cheerleader in vehicle at traffic light fell out

indicators.note: in places the selected letter inside the two-wheeled vehicle

parts.note: a bike is a two-wheeled vehicle
the leader of cheer is its first letter
a red traffic light means stop

explanation.surface: A cheerleader stuck in a car at a red light had an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheerleader' reads as one person; it is split into cheer and leader, giving the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To bicker is to quarrel over petty things, so bickered matches fell out, meaning argued.

clue.text: Harrow playboy

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a toothed farm implement for breaking up soil
second meaning: a dissolute pleasure-seeking man

explanation.walkthrough: Harrow is also a famous English public school, which makes the clue look like a description of a rich pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a toothed garden tool like a harrow and a dissolute man about town.

clue.text: Country doing badly — thousands at borders

indicators.note: at borders means on the outside edges, so the two thousand letters go either side

parts.note: K and M are both abbreviations for a thousand

indicators.note: badly means poorly done, so the letters of doing are jumbled

explanation.surface: A country is doing badly, with thousands massed on its borders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thousands' is plural because it gives two different letters that each mean a thousand.
explanation.definitionFit: A kingdom is a country ruled by a monarch, such as the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Skate possibly, one foot moving back in short bursts

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the turned letters go into the bursts

parts.note: flashes are short bursts, of light or feeling

indicators.note: moving back means going backwards, so one foot is read in reverse

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An ice skater moves one foot back in short bursts.
explanation.walkthrough: Skate is the fish here, not the skater the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Skate are flat-bodied fish, so a skate is one example of flatfishes, signalled by possibly.

clue.text: Doctor in Cape takes last of male testosterone, possibly

indicators.note: in tells us the medical man sits inside the headland

parts.note: Cape Horn, at the southern tip of South America
MO, medical officer

indicators.note: last of picks out the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the final letter

explanation.surface: A doctor in Cape Town treats a man with testosterone.
explanation.definitionFit: Testosterone is a hormone, a chemical messenger, so it is one example of the answer.

clue.text: Batter's happy with opening pair dropping down the order

indicators.text: with opening pair dropping down the order
indicators.note: the first two letters drop to the bottom, as an opening batting pair would drop down the batting order

parts.note: upbeat means cheerful

explanation.surface: A cricket batsman is pleased that the openers have moved lower in the batting order.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture makes 'Batter' a batsman; it is the verb meaning to beat. The first two letters of UPBEAT move to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat up is to assault someone violently, which is to batter them.

clue.text: Those who join protest fast

parts.note: surface reading: people who are quick to join any demonstration; setter's reading: fast is the verb meaning go without food, as a form of protest

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like an adverb meaning quickly; it is the verb meaning abstain from food.
explanation.definitionFit: People who refuse food as a protest are on a hunger strike, so they protest by fasting.

clue.text: Determination? King George needs it

parts.note: GR, Georgius Rex, King George's royal cipher
taken as written

explanation.surface: Does King George need determination?
explanation.definitionFit: Grit is courage and resolve, the strength of character to keep going, a synonym of determination.

clue.text: Thoroughly humiliated, Nixon retracted to some extent

indicators.note: retracted means drawn back, so the letters are read in reverse
to some extent means partly, so only part of the run of letters is used

parts.note: a run spanning the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Nixon, disgraced, withdrew his statements bit by bit.
explanation.walkthrough: Read humiLIATED NIxon backwards. Nixon retracting reminds of the Watergate scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in detail means covering every particular, that is, thoroughly.

clue.text: Passion's more difficult, they say, for East Enders

indicators.note: what they say is what is heard, so the word is taken by its sound
as said by Cockney Londoners, who drop the opening h of a word

parts.note: harder, with the h dropped in a Cockney accent

explanation.surface: Love is harder going for people living in London's East End.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, the traditional working-class Londoners of the East End, famously drop their h's; in a non-rhotic accent 'arder and ardour sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardour is intense enthusiasm or love, a fiery feeling that is a synonym of passion.

clue.text: Website for domestic servant?

parts.note: domestic means relating to home
a page is a boy servant

explanation.surface: A site advertising a household servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A home page is the main or starting page of a website, often standing for the whole site.

clue.text: Losing head, demure daughter's drunk most rum

indicators.note: drunk means swallowed, so the daughter letter is taken inside
losing head means without its first letter, so the word for demure loses its opening letter

parts.note: modest means demure
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A shy daughter drinks the most rum and loses her head.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum here means strange, not the drink the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum is a British word for odd or peculiar, so most rum means the strangest of all.
